title: Count the instructions
description:
The countdown program from the lesson looks like this, with the counter in cell 10 and the number one in cell 11:

| Cell | Instruction |
|---|---|
| 0 | `LOAD 10` |
| 1 | `JUMPZ 5` |
| 2 | `SUB 11` |
| 3 | `STORE 10` |
| 4 | `JUMP 1` |
| 5 | `HALT` |

Write `instructionsRun(start)`. It returns how many instructions the machine executes, from the first `LOAD` up to and including the `HALT`, when cell 10 starts at `start`.

Work it out on paper first: which instructions run once, and which run once per trip round the loop? Check your answer against the demonstration in the lesson, which counts instructions for you.

`start` is never negative.
hints: When the counter starts at 0, the machine runs `LOAD`, then `JUMPZ` (which jumps, because A is zero), then `HALT`. That is three instructions, and it is the part that always runs.
Each time the counter is not yet zero, four instructions run: `JUMPZ` (which does not jump), `SUB`, `STORE` and `JUMP`. So every extra count adds four.
The answer has the shape `4 * start + something`. Use the case where `start` is 0 to find the something.
lessonTitle: What Happens When a Program Runs
